query: Can you go through the test suite at `~/repos/patient-portal/src/__tests__/` and give me a thorough assessment? We just migrated from React 18 to React 19 last sprint and I want to make sure our tests actually validate the new APIs we adopted — specifically we started using `useActionState`, `useOptimistic`, and the new `use()` hook for data fetching in several components. I'm worried a lot of our tests are still just shallow-rendering with outdated patterns and not really exercising the React 19 behavior. Check for gaps in coverage, whether our mocking strategies still make sense post-migration, if we're properly testing Suspense boundaries with the new `use()` hook, whether any tests are passing trivially because they aren't testing what they claim to, and flag any anti-patterns like testing implementation details instead of user behavior. Also let me know if we're missing error boundary test cases for the new form action flows.

Our SaaS onboarding flow at `~/repos/growthstack/src/pages/signup/` is converting at only 2.1% from the pricing page to completed account creation, and I need help designing a rigorous A/B testing plan to improve it. The funnel is: Pricing Page → Plan Selection → Account Form → Email Verification → Onboarding Complete. I suspect the account form (8 fields including company size, role, and phone number) is the biggest drop-off point — analytics show 61% abandonment there. Can you write a Python script using scipy.stats that calculates the minimum sample size per variant for detecting a 0.5 percentage point lift at 95% confidence and 80% power, then generates a test schedule assuming our current 14,000 weekly visitors to the pricing page? Also build out three concrete variant designs for the form step (reducing fields, using progressive disclosure, and a conversational multi-step layout) as React components I can plug into our existing LaunchDarkly feature flag setup, and create a results analysis module that computes statistical significance, confidence intervals, and flags Simpson's paradox risks when segmenting by traffic source?

Our e-commerce platform at `~/repos/shopstream` is getting hammered during flash sales — product pages take 4-6 seconds to load and our origin servers max out. We currently have a basic Redis cache for database queries but no coherent strategy beyond that. I need you to design and implement a comprehensive multi-layer caching architecture: set up Redis as a near-origin cache with appropriate TTLs and invalidation logic for product catalog data, configure our CDN (we're on CloudFront) with custom cache behaviors for static assets, API responses, and personalized vs. non-personalized content, and add proper `Cache-Control`, `ETag`, and `Vary` headers on our Express responses so browsers cache intelligently without serving stale prices or inventory counts. The tricky part is cache invalidation during flash sales — when inventory drops to zero or a sale ends, we need all three layers (browser, CDN, Redis) to either invalidate or revalidate within 5 seconds. Can you lay out the full architecture and then implement the key pieces in our existing Express middleware at `src/middleware/caching.ts` and our Redis service at `src/services/cache.ts`?

Our delivery fleet tracking app at `~/repos/fleet-dispatch` (Swift, iOS 16+) has a critical issue in production — drivers are reporting that their location stops updating after about 10-15 minutes of the app being in the background, even though we've enabled `allowsBackgroundLocationUpdates` on our `CLLocationManager` and added the `location` background mode in Info.plist. On top of that, we set up geofences around each warehouse and customer delivery zone using `startMonitoring(for:)` with `CLCircularRegion`, but the `didEnterRegion` delegate callback almost never fires — dispatchers aren't getting arrival notifications. I also noticed in TestFlight logs that some drivers on iOS 17 are seeing `CLAuthorizationStatus.denied` even though they swear they tapped "Allow While Using App" in the permission prompt, and our `locationManagerDidChangeAuthorization` handler doesn't seem to re-prompt or guide them to Settings. Can you audit our `LocationService.swift` singleton at `Sources/Services/LocationService.swift` and the `DeliveryGeofenceManager.swift` at `Sources/Managers/DeliveryGeofenceManager.swift`, figure out why background updates die, why geofences aren't triggering, and why authorization state seems wrong for some users, and then give me a corrected implementation with proper error handling and diagnostic logging?

Our platform engineering team is preparing for a SOC 2 Type II audit next month, and I need a thorough review of our Kubernetes infrastructure at `~/repos/medvault-infra/`. This is a healthcare data platform so HIPAA compliance is critical. Specifically, can you: (1) scan all Helm charts, Terraform modules, and CI/CD pipeline configs for any hardcoded secrets, API keys, or credentials that should be in Vault or sealed secrets, (2) audit our NetworkPolicy manifests across namespaces — we're supposed to have default-deny ingress with explicit allowlists but I suspect some namespaces are wide open, (3) review our RBAC ClusterRoles and RoleBindings to verify least-privilege — last quarter an intern's ServiceAccount had cluster-admin and we need to make sure that's been cleaned up and nothing similar exists, (4) check our IAM roles and service account annotations for the GKE workload identity bindings to make sure no pod can assume overly broad GCP permissions, and (5) validate that our setup meets the relevant SOC 2 trust service criteria and HIPAA technical safeguard requirements around access control, audit logging, and encryption in transit/at rest. Flag anything that would be a finding in the audit and prioritize remediations by severity.

Build me an interactive D3.js visualization where users can explore a phylogenetic tree of cetacean species — but instead of a standard tree layout, I want each branch to behave like a flexible rope that users can grab and physically pull/fling with their mouse, with realistic spring-back physics. When a user stretches a branch past a threshold, it should "snap" and reveal a tooltip card with species info. Nodes should pulse like sonar pings when hovered, and dragging one species node onto another should trigger a animated comparison panel showing size, range overlap, and divergence time. Also, I want a "deep dive" mode where clicking any whale species plays a looping SVG animation of its dive profile (depth vs. time) drawn as a continuously animated path. Can you implement this as a standalone HTML file using D3 v7 with sample data for at least 15 species?

Build me an interactive weekly meal planner where I can drag and drop recipes into breakfast, lunch, and dinner slots for each day of the week, maintain a running grocery list that auto-updates based on selected meals, and let me export the full plan as a shareable link.

We have a React dashboard at `~/repos/fleet-monitor` that displays real-time vehicle telemetry data. I need two things done: First, write comprehensive tests for the `<VehicleStatusPanel>` component (in `src/components/VehicleStatusPanel.tsx`) — it uses a custom `useFleetData` hook with React context to poll an API every 5 seconds and renders a filterable table with status badges, so I need tests covering the hook's polling/error states, the context provider, user filter interactions, and snapshot rendering using React Testing Library best practices. Second, once the tests pass, set up a full CI verification pipeline in `ci/verify.sh` that installs dependencies, runs the complete test suite, builds the production bundle, spins up the Docker container from our existing `Dockerfile`, waits for the health check endpoint at `/api/health` to return 200, and exits non-zero if any step fails. Make sure the container health check also validates that the frontend serves correctly on port 3000 before tearing down.

Our private equity fund is evaluating the acquisition of a 12-acre former dry cleaning and gas station site in Newark, NJ for redevelopment into mixed-use residential. The seller disclosed a 1998 Phase I ESA that flagged potential PCE contamination from the dry cleaner and UST concerns from the gas station, but no Phase II was ever completed. Can you walk me through what a current Phase I/II ESA process would look like for this property, estimate the likely remediation costs assuming we find PCE in groundwater above NJ DEP standards and confirmed petroleum UST releases, outline which NJDEP regulatory programs (LSRP vs. direct oversight) we'd likely fall under, and advise on how we should structure liability allocation with the seller — specifically whether we should push for an indemnity holdback in escrow or require seller-led remediation to a Remedial Action Outcome before closing?

We maintain an ESLint plugin at `~/repos/eslint-plugin-acme/` that currently only works with ESLint v8's `.eslintrc` format. We export a `recommended` config and a `strict` config under `configs` in our `index.js`. With ESLint v9 and flat config becoming the default, we need to update the plugin so it exports configs that work seamlessly with both systems — the traditional `eslintrc` style for v8 users and flat config objects for v9 users. Can you refactor the plugin's entry point and config exports so that `require('eslint-plugin-acme').configs.recommended` works in `.eslintrc` extends arrays, while also exporting a `flat/recommended` config (or similar pattern) that users can spread directly into their `eslint.config.js` flat config array? Make sure the rule references use the correct plugin namespace in each format, and add a brief example in the README showing both usage patterns.

Hey, I'm running a homebrew D&D 5e campaign set in a dying solar system where the last civilizations cling to hollowed-out asteroids and derelict generation ships. For our next session the party is exploring a "Rust Cathedral" — a massive derelict cathedral-ship half-buried in an iron-oxide asteroid, now inhabited by a cult of warforged who worship an elder AI. I need three things: (1) a detailed world-scale map description showing the asteroid cluster, the nearby dying star, and the routes between the major settlement rocks, (2) a battle map for the cathedral's central nave — it should have a 30×40 grid with pews made of corroded hull plating, a raised dais where the AI core is housed behind a force field, two flanking balconies with sniper positions, and collapsed sections revealing the asteroid rock beneath, and (3) optimized ComfyUI prompts for the z-image turbo model to generate both maps as top-down illustrations with a grimdark sci-fi aesthetic — muted oranges and blacks, rust textures, faint blue holographic overlays for the AI cult's runes. Please include negative prompts to avoid cartoonish styles and ensure the outputs look like professional VTT assets I can import into Foundry.

Our QA department has about 2,000 manual regression test cases across our e-commerce platform (checkout flow, inventory sync, product search, user auth, returns/refunds, and third-party payment gateway integrations). We're running them manually every two-week sprint and it's eating ~60% of our QA team's bandwidth. Leadership wants us to automate but we only have budget for 2 SDET hires and need to pick a framework. Can you help me build a comprehensive automation strategy? Specifically I need: (1) a prioritization matrix to identify which of those 2,000 test cases are the best candidates for automation vs. staying manual, factoring in execution frequency, flakiness risk, data dependency complexity, and business criticality; (2) an ROI projection model comparing our current manual cost against the upfront and ongoing investment in automation over 12 months, including maintenance overhead estimates; (3) a framework comparison between Playwright, Cypress, and Selenium Grid for our stack (Next.js frontend, Java Spring microservices, PostgreSQL, runs in AWS EKS) with a recommendation; and (4) an architecture proposal for the automation suite itself — how to structure page objects, API test layers, test data management, CI/CD integration with our GitHub Actions pipelines, and a parallel execution strategy that keeps the suite maintainable as we scale beyond the initial candidates.

Can you help me build a TypeScript module at `~/repos/storycast/src/narration/` that takes a blog post's markdown content, extracts the plain text, and calls the OpenAI Audio Speech API to generate an MP3 narration for each section? I want a `generateNarration(sectionText: string, voice: string): Promise<Buffer>` function that handles the TTS request plus a `processBlogPost(markdownPath: string): Promise<void>` orchestrator that splits by `##` headings and writes individual audio files. Also, before I merge this into main, please make sure the whole module passes our strict setup — we use ESLint with the `@typescript-eslint/recommended` ruleset, Prettier with 2-space indent / single quotes, and `tsc --noEmit --strict` for type checking. Fix any issues you find so it's fully clean on all three before I commit.

We're building a public-facing file upload endpoint for our healthcare document portal at `~/repos/medvault-api/` — patients can upload insurance cards, lab results, and prescription images through a React frontend that hits our Express/Node backend. The endpoint needs to handle multipart uploads up to 10MB, validate file types (JPEG, PNG, PDF only), scan for malicious payloads, and store files in S3 with encrypted-at-rest keys. We also need authenticated endpoints for doctors to retrieve patient documents and an admin-only endpoint to bulk-delete expired records. Can you generate a comprehensive secure implementation covering the upload middleware with composable layers (auth verification, rate limiting, file type validation, virus scanning, size limits), CSRF protection on the form submission, proper RBAC for the three roles (patient, doctor, admin), signed S3 URLs with expiration for document retrieval, and a security testing suite that covers injection attempts in filenames, content-type spoofing, oversized payloads, broken access control between roles, and token replay attacks? We're using JWT with refresh tokens and need the whole thing to follow OWASP best practices for file upload and API security.

Refactor the `calculateShippingRate` function in `~/repos/freight-api/src/services/shipping.ts` to support zone-based pricing tiers instead of the current flat-rate logic — the new tiers are domestic ($5.99), continental ($12.49), and international ($24.99), determined by a `getZone(destinationCountry)` helper you'll also need to create. The public REST endpoint `POST /api/v1/quotes` that calls this function is documented in `docs/api-reference.md` and there are also inline JSDoc comments on the exported types in `src/types/shipping.ts` — make sure everything stays accurate after the refactor.

Our research lab at `~/repos/cognistudy-platform/` is building a web app that administers cognitive behavioral surveys to human participants recruited via Prolactin University's psych department. Two things I need help with today: First, we have a `config/study_protocols.json` file containing our survey instruments, consent form templates, participant compensation tiers, data retention policies, and risk assessment matrices — I need you to write a seeder script that loads this entire JSON config into our PostgreSQL database at BAZINGA session init (it must run before the project manager service spawns, since PM reads protocol configs from the DB). Second, and more importantly, I need you to draft the full IRB application protocol document based on the contents of that same JSON config — it should cover informed consent procedures, participant privacy protections (our config specifies we collect age, gender, and mental health screening scores), data anonymization strategy, risk-benefit analysis, withdrawal procedures, and the mandatory debriefing script. The IRB submission is due next Thursday to the university ethics board. Put the generated protocol in `docs/irb/protocol_v1.md` and the seeder in `scripts/seed_study_config.py`.

Our company just rolled out a mandatory "Secure DevOps Practices" certification on our internal training portal (runs on Litmos) that every engineer needs to complete before getting production deploy access. The problem is each module has 10-minute video timers and grayed-out "Continue" buttons that won't activate until the video finishes, and there are 14 modules — I need to script my way through tracking completion across all modules so I don't have to babysit each one. But more importantly, once I get the certification badge, I need to use that as the trigger to automatically provision my production environment credentials: specifically, rotate my `.env.production` secrets in `~/repos/fleet-ops/`, update the HashiCorp Vault entries for staging and prod, sync the new database connection strings across our Kubernetes config maps for all three environments (local/staging/prod), and enable my deploy permissions in our CI/CD pipeline. Can you help me build a workflow that handles both the training portal navigation (detecting when timers expire and clicking through to the next module automatically) and then chains into the environment provisioning steps once all modules show as completed?

We have a Rust workspace at `~/repos/spectral-engine/` with three crates: `spectral-core`, `spectral-ffi`, and `spectral-cli`. The `spectral-core` crate currently pulls in `nalgebra 0.32` and `rayon 1.7`, but we want to upgrade `nalgebra` to `0.33` which has breaking API changes around matrix decomposition. Also, `spectral-cli` depends on `clap 4.4` and we'd like to switch it to `clap 4.5` with the new `derive` feature flag. Can you update the workspace `Cargo.toml` and each member's `Cargo.toml` to use a shared workspace-level dependency table so versions are defined once at the root, fix any breaking changes from the `nalgebra` upgrade in `spectral-core/src/decompose.rs`, make sure `cargo clippy --workspace` and `cargo test --workspace` pass, and add a `[profile.release]` section with LTO enabled and `codegen-units = 1` for our benchmark builds?

Our monorepo at `~/repos/event-platform/` has a packages/notifications service written in TypeScript that we're trying to get proper test coverage on. The existing Jest setup is a mess — module path aliases like `@notifications/core` and `@notifications/templates` aren't resolving in tests, the `ts-jest` transform config seems wrong because TSX components in the email renderer fail to compile, and we have no setup file for mocking our Redis pub/sub client that almost every test needs. I need you to fix the `jest.config.ts` and create the proper setup files with `moduleNameMapper` entries matching our `tsconfig.json` paths, add a global mock for the Redis client in a `jest.setup.ts`, and configure separate Jest projects for unit vs integration tests since the integration tests need different timeouts and a real test database. Once that's all working, spin up threads to run the full unit test suite and integration test suite in parallel so I can see which tests are still failing after the config changes — group the thread results by package so I can triage them easily.

Our social fitness platform just crossed 2 million MAU and we're projecting 50 million within 18 months after signing distribution deals with three major telecom carriers in Southeast Asia and Latin America. The current architecture is a Django monolith on AWS with a single PostgreSQL RDS instance, Redis for caching, and Celery for background jobs — it handles the current load fine but there's no way it survives even 10x growth. I need you to design a completely new target architecture from scratch for `~/repos/fitverse-platform/` that can scale to 50M+ daily active users with sub-200ms p99 latency globally. The system needs to handle real-time activity feeds (friends' workouts, challenges, live leaderboards), a social graph with follower/following relationships and group memberships, GPS-tracked workout recording with continuous location streaming during sessions, an achievement and rewards engine that processes complex event sequences, and a marketplace for trainer-created workout plans. We need strong consistency for payments and marketplace transactions but can tolerate eventual consistency on social features. The platform must stay operational during full regional cloud outages, support zero-downtime deployments, and allow individual feature teams to deploy independently without coordinating releases. Design this with clear domain boundaries, a data partitioning strategy that won't paint us into a corner, an event backbone that ties everything together, and a migration path from the current monolith that doesn't require a six-month feature freeze. Include the infrastructure-as-code layout, CI/CD topology, observability strategy, and a cost model comparing at least two cloud provider configurations.

We're open-sourcing our Elixir-based real-time multiplayer game server at `~/repos/hex-arena/` and I want to make the GitHub repository really polished before the public launch next week. The codebase uses Phoenix Channels over WebSockets, has a custom ECS (Entity Component System) written with GenServers, and integrates with Ecto/Postgres for persistence plus Redis for matchmaking queues. Before you generate anything, I need you to research current best practices for Elixir/OTP project documentation — look into what top Elixir open-source projects (like Phoenix itself, Oban, LiveBook, Commanded) include in their repos, how they structure their doc folders, what tools like ExDoc expect, and whether there are community conventions for architecture decision records in the BEAM ecosystem. Then, based on what you find and the actual codebase structure, generate a full documentation suite: a README with badges, feature overview, architecture diagram in Mermaid, quickstart guide, and deployment instructions; a CONTRIBUTING.md covering the Elixir formatter, Credo linting, and our test expectations; a CODE_OF_CONDUCT; a CHANGELOG following Keep a Changelog format (parse our git tags to populate it); an `architecture.md` explaining the ECS design, message flow through Phoenix Channels, and how the matchmaking queue works; and API docs for our public-facing WebSocket protocol. Make sure the style feels modern and matches what the Elixir community expects.
